subparagraph.content: Establishment of such legal and institutional structures as are necessary to ensure the effective long-term operation of the project by the non-Federal interest.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Federal share of the cost of a project under this section—

clause.content: shall be 75 percent; and
may be provided in the form of grants or reimbursements of project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for work.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall credit, in accordance with section 221 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d–5b), toward the non-Federal share of the cost of the project the cost of design work carried out by the non-Federal interest for the project before the date of the partnership agreement for the project.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for interest.—
subparagraph.content: In case of a delay in the funding of the non-Federal share of the costs of a project that is the subject of an agreement under this section, the non-Federal interest shall receive credit for reasonable interest incurred in providing the non-Federal share.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for land, easements, and rights-of-way.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal interest shall receive credit for land, easements, rights-of-way, and relocations toward the non-Federal share of project costs (including all reasonable costs associated with obtaining permits necessary for the construction, operation, and maintenance of the project on publicly owned or controlled land), but the credit may not exceed 25 percent of total project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Operation and maintenance.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal share of operation and maintenance costs for projects constructed with assistance provided under this section shall be 100 percent.

subsection.heading: Applicability of Other Federal and State Laws.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section shall be construed to waive, limit, or otherwise affect the applicability of any provision of Federal or State law that would otherwise apply to a project to be carried out with assistance provided under this section.

subsection.heading: Nonprofit Entities.—
subsection.content: In accordance with section 221(b) of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d–5b(b)), for any project carried out under this section, a non-Federal interest may include a nonprofit entity.

subsection.heading: Corps of Engineers Expenses.—
subsection.content: Not more than 10 percent of amounts made available to carry out this section may be used by the Corps of Engineers district offices to administer projects under this section at Federal expense.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $40,000,000.

section.heading: CALAVERAS RIVER AND LITTLEJOHN CREEK AND TRIBUTARIES, STOCKTON, CALIFORNIA.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: Unless the Secretary determines, by not later than 30 days after the date of enactment of this Act, that the relocation of the portion of the project described in subsection (b)(2) would be injurious to the public interest, a non-Federal interest may reconstruct and relocate that portion of the project approximately 300 feet in a westerly direction.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The project referred to in subsection (a) is the project for flood control, Calaveras River and Littlejohn Creek and tributaries, California, authorized by section 10 of the Flood Control Act of December 22, 1944 (58 Stat. 902).

paragraph.heading: Specific description.—
paragraph.content: The portion of the project to be reconstructed and relocated is that portion consisting of approximately 5.34 acres of dry land levee beginning at a point N. 2203542.3167, E. 6310930.1385, thence running west about 59.99 feet to a point N. 2203544.6562, E. 6310870.1468, thence running south about 3,874.99 feet to a point N. 2199669.8760, E. 6310861.7956, thence running east about 60.00 feet to a point N. 2199668.8026, E. 6310921.7900, thence running north about 3,873.73 feet to the point of origin.

subsection.heading: Cost Sharing.—
subsection.content: The non-Federal share of the cost of reconstructing and relocating the portion of the project described in subsection (b)(2) shall be 100 percent.

subsection.chapeau: Section 219(f)(48) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1992 (114 Stat. 2763A–220) is amended—

paragraph.content:
by adding at the end the following:
“(B) Credit.—The Secretary shall credit, in accordance with section 221 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d–5b), toward the non-Federal share of the cost of the project not to exceed $3,000,000 for the cost of planning and design work carried out by the non-Federal interest for the project before the date of the partnership agreement for the project.” ; and
by aligning the remainder of the text of subparagraph (A) (as designated by paragraph (1) of this section) with subparagraph (B) (as added by paragraph (2) of this section).

section.heading: CONTRA COSTA CANAL, OAKLEY AND KNIGHTSEN, CALIFORNIA; MALLARD SLOUGH, PITTSBURG, CALIFORNIA.
section.content: Sections 512 and 514 of the Water Resources Development Act of 2000 (114 Stat. 2650) are each amended by adding at the end the following: “All planning, study, design, and construction on the project shall be carried out by the office of the district engineer, San Francisco, California.”.

section.heading: DANA POINT HARBOR, CALIFORNIA.
section.content: The Secretary shall conduct a study of the causes of water quality degradation within Dana Point Harbor, California, to determine if the degradation is the result of a Federal navigation project, and, if the Secretary determines that the degradation is the result of a Federal navigation project, the Secretary shall carry out a project to mitigate the degradation at Federal expense.

subsection.chapeau: Section 219(f)(22) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1992 (113 Stat. 336) is amended—

paragraph.content:
by adding at the end the following:
“(B) Credit.—The Secretary shall credit, in accordance with section 221 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d–5b), toward the non-Federal share of the cost of the project the cost of design and construction work carried out by the non-Federal interest for the project before the date of the partnership agreement for the project.
“(C) In-kind contributions.—The non-Federal interest may provide any portion of the non-Federal share of the cost of the project in the form of in-kind services and materials.” ; and
by aligning the remainder of the text of subparagraph (A) (as designated by paragraph (1) of this section) with subparagraph (B) (as added by paragraph (2) of this section).

subsection.chapeau: Section 111(c) of the Miscellaneous Appropriations Act, 2001 (as enacted into law by Public Law 106–554; 114 Stat. 2763A–224) is amended—

paragraph.content: by striking “$25,000,000” and inserting “$28,000,000”; and
by striking “$7,000,000” and inserting “$10,000,000”.

section.heading: LA–3 DREDGED MATERIAL OCEAN DISPOSAL SITE DESIGNATION, CALIFORNIA.
section.content: The third sentence of section 102(c)(4) of the Marine Protection, Research, and Sanctuaries Act of 1972 (33 U.S.C. 1412(c)(4)) is amended by striking “January 1, 2003” and inserting “January 1, 2011”.

subsection.chapeau: Section 219(f)(50) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1992 (114 Stat. 2763A–220) is amended—

paragraph.content: by inserting after “water” the following: “and wastewater”; and
by striking “$14,500,000” and inserting “$24,500,000”.

section.heading: LOS OSOS, CALIFORNIA.
section.content:
Section 219(c)(27) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1992 (114 Stat. 2763A–219) is amended to read as follows:
“(27) Los osos, california.—Wastewater infrastructure, Los Osos, California.” .

section.heading: PINE FLAT DAM FISH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT, CALIFORNIA.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall participate with appropriate State and local agencies in the implementation of a cooperative program to improve and manage fisheries and aquatic habitat conditions in Pine Flat Reservoir and in the 14-mile reach of the Kings River immediately below Pine Flat Dam, California, in a manner that—

subparagraph.content: provides for long-term aquatic resource enhancement; and
avoids adverse effects on water storage and water rights holders.

paragraph.heading: Goals and principles.—
paragraph.chapeau: The cooperative program described in paragraph (1) shall be carried out—

subparagraph.content: substantially in accordance with the goals and principles of the document entitled “Kings River Fisheries Management Program Framework Agreement” and dated May 29, 1999, between the California department of fish and game and the Kings River Water Association and the Kings River Conservation District; and
in cooperation with the parties to that agreement.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: In furtherance of the goals of the agreement described in subsection (a)(2), the Secretary shall participate in the planning, design, and construction of projects and pilot projects on the Kings River and its tributaries to enhance aquatic habitat and water availability for fisheries purposes (including maintenance of a trout fishery) in accordance with flood control operations, water rights, and beneficial uses in existence as of the date of enactment of this Act.

paragraph.heading: Projects.—
paragraph.chapeau: Projects referred to in paragraph (1) may include—

subparagraph.content: projects to construct or improve pumping, conveyance, and storage facilities to enhance water transfers; and
projects to carry out water exchanges and create opportunities to use floodwater within and downstream of Pine Flat Reservoir.

subsection.heading: No Authorization of Certain Dam-Related Projects.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section shall be construed to authorize any project for the raising of Pine Flat Dam or the construction of a multilevel intake structure at Pine Flat Dam.

subsection.heading: Use of Existing Studies.—
subsection.content: In carrying out this section, the Secretary shall use, to the maximum extent practicable, studies in existence on the date of enactment of this Act, including data and environmental documentation in the document entitled “Final Feasibility Report and Report of the Chief of Engineers for Pine Flat Dam Fish and Wildlife Habitat Restoration” and dated July 19, 2002.

subsection.heading: Credit for Land, Easements, and Rights-of-Way.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall credit toward the non-Federal share of the cost of construction of any project under subsection (b) the value, regardless of the date of acquisition, of any land, easements, rights-of-way, dredged material disposal areas, or relocations provided by the non-Federal interest for use in carrying out the project.

subsection.heading: Operation and Maintenance.—
subsection.content: The operation, maintenance, repair, rehabilitation, and replacement of projects carried out under this section shall be a non-Federal responsibility.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $20,000,000. Such sums shall remain available until expended.

section.heading: RAYMOND BASIN, SIX BASINS, CHINO BASIN, AND SAN GABRIEL BASIN, CALIFORNIA.

subsection.heading: Comprehensive Plan.—
subsection.content: The Secretary, in consultation and coordination with appropriate Federal, State, and local entities, shall develop a comprehensive plan for the management of water resources in the Raymond Basin, Six Basins, Chino Basin, and San Gabriel Basin, California. The Secretary may carry out activities identified in the comprehensive plan to demonstrate practicable alternatives for water resources management.

subsection.heading: Operation and Maintenance.—
subsection.content: The non-Federal share of the cost of operation and maintenance of any measures constructed under this section shall be 100 percent.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $5,000,000.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary, in cooperation with the Port of San Francisco, California, may carry out the project for repair and removal, as appropriate, of Piers 30–32, 35, 36, 70 (including Wharves 7 and 8), and 80 in San Francisco, California, substantially in accordance with the Port's redevelopment plan.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriation.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated $25,000,000 to carry out this section.

title.editorialNote: [Section 5052 of this Act was repealed by section 316(b) of division AA of Public Law 116–260.]

section.heading: SAN PABLO BAY, CALIFORNIA, WATERSHED AND SUISUN MARSH ECOSYSTEM RESTORATION.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall complete work, as expeditiously as possible, on the ongoing San Pablo Bay watershed, California, study to determine the feasibility of opportunities for restoring, preserving, and protecting the San Pablo Bay watershed.

paragraph.heading: Report.—
paragraph.content: Not later than March 31, 2008, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report on the results of the study.

subsection.heading: Suisun Marsh, California.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall conduct a comprehensive study to determine the feasibility of opportunities for restoring, preserving, and protecting the Suisun Marsh, California.

subsection.heading: San Pablo and Suisun Bay Marsh Watershed Critical Restoration Projects.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary may participate in critical restoration projects that will produce, consistent with Federal programs, projects, and activities, immediate and substantial ecosystem restoration, preservation, and protection benefits in the following sub-watersheds of the San Pablo and Suisun Bay Marsh watersheds:

subparagraph.content: The tidal areas of the Petaluma River, Napa-Sonoma Marsh.
The shoreline of West Contra Costa County.
Novato Creek.
Suisun Marsh.
Gallinas-Miller Creek.

paragraph.heading: Types of assistance.—
paragraph.content: Participation in critical restoration projects under this subsection may include assistance for planning, design, or construction.

subsection.heading: Credit.—
subsection.chapeau: In accordance with section 221 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d–5b), the Secretary shall credit toward the non-Federal share of the cost of construction of a project under this section—

paragraph.content: the value of any lands, easements, rights-of-way, dredged material disposal areas, or relocations provided by the non-Federal interest for carrying out the project, regardless of the date of acquisition;
funds received from the CALFED Bay-Delta program; and
the cost of the studies, design, and construction work carried out by the non-Federal interest before the date of the partnership agreement for the project.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $40,000,000.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may construct a project for flood control and environmental restoration, St. Helena, California, substantially in accordance with the plan for the St. Helena comprehensive flood protection project dated 2006 and described in the addendum dated June 27, 2006, to the report prepared by the city of St. Helena entitled “City of St. Helena Comprehensive Flood Protection Project, Final Environmental Impact Report”, and dated January 2004, if the Secretary determines that the plans and designs for the project are feasible.

subsection.heading: Cost.—
subsection.content: The total cost of the project to be constructed pursuant to subsection (a) shall be $30,000,000, with an estimated Federal cost of $19,500,000 and an estimated non-Federal cost of $10,500,000.

subsection.heading: Reimbursement.—
subsection.content: The non-Federal interest shall be reimbursed for any work performed by the non-Federal interest for the project described in subsection (a) that is in excess of the required non-Federal contribution toward the total cost of the project, if the Secretary determines that the work is integral to the project.

subsection.heading: Reevaluation.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall reevaluate the feasibility of the Lower Mosher Slough element and the levee extensions on the Upper Calaveras River element of the project for flood control, Stockton Metropolitan Area, California, carried out under section 211(f)(3) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1996 (110 Stat. 3683), to determine the eligibility of such elements for reimbursement under section 211 of such Act (33 U.S.C. 701b–13).

subsection.heading: Special Rules for Reevaluation.—
subsection.content: In conducting the reevaluation under subsection (a), the Secretary shall not reject a feasibility determination based on one or more of the policies of the Corps of Engineers concerning the frequency of flooding, the drainage area, and the amount of runoff.

subsection.heading: Reimbursement.—
subsection.content: If the Secretary determines that the elements referred to subsection (a) are feasible, the Secretary shall reimburse, subject to appropriations, the non-Federal interest under section 211 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1996 for the Federal share of the cost of such elements.

section.heading: RIO GRANDE ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT PROGRAM, COLORADO, NEW MEXICO, AND TEXAS.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section, the following definitions apply:

paragraph.heading: Rio grande compact.—
paragraph.content: The term “Rio Grande Compact” means the compact approved by Congress under the Act of May 31, 1939 (53 Stat. 785), and ratified by the States.

paragraph.heading: Rio grande basin.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “Rio Grande Basin” means the Rio Grande (including all tributaries and their headwaters) located—

subparagraph.content: in the State of Colorado, from the Rio Grande Reservoir, near Creede, Colorado, to the New Mexico State border;
in the State of New Mexico, from the Colorado State border downstream to the Texas State border; and
in the State of Texas, from the New Mexico State border to the southern terminus of the Rio Grande at the Gulf of Mexico.

paragraph.heading: States.—
paragraph.content: The term “States” means the States of Colorado, New Mexico, and Texas.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall carry out, in the Rio Grande Basin—

subparagraph.content: a program for the planning, construction, and evaluation of measures for fish and wildlife habitat rehabilitation and enhancement; and
implementation of a long-term monitoring, computerized data inventory and analysis, applied research, and adaptive management program.

paragraph.heading: Reports.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than December 31, 2014, and not later than December 31 of every sixth year thereafter, the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of the Interior and the States, shall submit to Congress a report that—

subparagraph.content: contains an evaluation of the programs described in paragraph (1);
describes the accomplishments of each program;
provides updates of a systemic habitat needs assessment and an assessment of needs for other related purposes in the Rio Grande Basin, including flood damage reduction; and
identifies any needed adjustments in the authorization of the programs.

subsection.heading: State and Local Consultation and Cooperative Effort.—
subsection.chapeau: For the purpose of ensuring the coordinated planning and implementation of the programs described in subsection (b), the Secretary shall—

paragraph.content: consult with the States, and other appropriate entities in the States, the rights and interests of which might be affected by specific program activities; and

enter into 1 or more interagency agreements with the Secretary of State and the Secretary of the Interior to provide for the direct participation of, and transfer of funds to, the United States Fish and Wildlife Service and any other agency or bureau of the Department of the Interior or the U.S. Section of the International Boundary and Water Commission for the planning, design, implementation, and evaluation of those programs.

subsection.heading: Operation and Maintenance.—
subsection.content: The costs of operation and maintenance of a project located on Federal land, or land owned or operated by a State or local government, shall be borne by the Federal, State, or local agency that has jurisdiction over fish and wildlife activities on the land.

paragraph.heading: Water law.—
paragraph.content: Nothing in this section shall be construed to preempt any State water law.

paragraph.heading: Compacts and decrees.—
paragraph.content: In carrying out this section, the Secretary shall comply with the Rio Grande Compact, and any applicable court decrees or Federal and State laws, affecting water or water rights in the Rio Grande Basin.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section $15,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2029.

section.heading: CHARLES HERVEY TOWNSHEND BREAKWATER, NEW HAVEN HARBOR, CONNECTICUT.
section.content: The western breakwater for the project for navigation, New Haven Harbor, Connecticut, authorized by the first section of the Act of September 19, 1890 (26 Stat. 428), shall be known and designated as the “Charles Hervey Townshend Breakwater”.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may participate in the ecosystem restoration, navigation, flood damage reduction, and recreation components of the Mill River and Long Island Sound revitalization project, Stamford, Connecticut.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated $10,000,000 to carry out this section.

title.editorialNote: [Section 5059 was repealed by section 2811(b) of Public Law 115-334.]

section.heading: ANACOSTIA RIVER, DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA AND MARYLAND.

subsection.heading: Comprehensive Action Plan.—
subsection.content: Not later than one year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary, in coordination with the Mayor of the District of Columbia, the Governor of Maryland, the county executives of Montgomery County and Prince George's County, Maryland, and other interested entities, shall develop and make available to the public a 10-year comprehensive action plan to provide for the restoration and protection of the ecological integrity of the Anacostia River and its tributaries.

subsection.heading: Public Availability.—
subsection.content: On completion of the comprehensive action plan under subsection (a), the Secretary shall make the plan available to the public, including on the Internet.

subsection.heading: East Central and Northeast Florida Region Defined.—
subsection.content: In this section, the term “East Central and Northeast Florida Region” means Flagler County, St. Johns County, Putman County (east of the St. Johns River), Seminole County, Volusia County, the towns of Winter Park, Maitland, and Palatka, Florida.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Program.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may establish a program to provide environmental assistance to non-Federal interests in the East Central and Northeast Florida Region.

subsection.heading: Form of Assistance.—
subsection.content: Assistance provided under this section may be in the form of design and construction assistance for water-related environmental infrastructure and resource protection and development projects in the East Central and Northeast Florida Region, including projects for wastewater treatment and related facilities, water supply and related facilities, environmental restoration, and surface water resource protection and development.

subsection.heading: Ownership Requirement.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may provide assistance for a project under this section only if the project is publicly owned.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Before providing assistance under this section, the Secretary shall enter into a partnership agreement with a non-Federal interest to provide for design and construction of the project to be carried out with the assistance.

paragraph.heading: Requirements.—
paragraph.chapeau: Each partnership agreement for a project entered into under this subsection shall provide for the following:

subparagraph.heading: Plan.—
subparagraph.content: Development by the Secretary, in consultation with appropriate Federal and State officials, of a facilities or resource protection and development plan, including appropriate engineering plans and specifications.

subparagraph.heading: Legal and institutional structures.—
subparagraph.content: Establishment of such legal and institutional structures as are necessary to ensure the effective long-term operation of the project by the non-Federal interest.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Federal share of the cost of a project under this section—

clause.content: shall be 75 percent; and
may be provided in the form of grants or reimbursements of project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for work.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall credit, in accordance with section 221 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d–5b), toward the non-Federal share of the cost of the project the cost of design work carried out by the non-Federal interest for the project before the date of the partnership agreement for the project.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for interest.—
subparagraph.content: In case of a delay in the funding of the non-Federal share of the costs of a project that is the subject of an agreement under this section, the non-Federal interest shall receive credit for reasonable interest incurred in providing the non-Federal share.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for land, easements, and rights-of-way.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal interest shall receive credit for land, easements, rights-of-way, and relocations toward the non-Federal share of project costs (including all reasonable costs associated with obtaining permits necessary for the construction, operation, and maintenance of the project on publicly owned or controlled land), but the credit may not exceed 25 percent of total project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Operation and maintenance.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal share of operation and maintenance costs for projects constructed with assistance provided under this section shall be 100 percent.

subsection.heading: Applicability of Other Federal and State Laws.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section shall be construed to waive, limit, or otherwise affect the applicability of any provision of Federal or State law that would otherwise apply to a project to be carried out with assistance provided under this section.

subsection.heading: Nonprofit Entities.—
subsection.content: In accordance with section 221(b) of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d–5b(b)), for any project carried out under this section, a non-Federal interest may include a nonprofit entity with the consent of the affected local government.

subsection.heading: Corps of Engineers Expenses.—
subsection.content: Not more than 10 percent of the amounts appropriated to carry out this section may be used by the Corps of Engineers district offices to administer projects under this section at Federal expense.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $40,000,000.

subsection.chapeau: Section 109 of the Miscellaneous Appropriations Act, 2001 (enacted into law by Public Law 106–554) (114 Stat. 2763A–222) is amended—

paragraph.content:
by adding at the end of subsection (e)(2) the following:
“(C) Credit for work prior to execution of the partnership agreement.—The Secretary shall credit toward the non-Federal share of the cost of the project—
“(i) in accordance with section 221 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d–5b), the cost of construction work carried out by the non-Federal interest for the project before the date of the partnership agreement for the project; and
“(ii) the cost of land acquisition carried out by the non-Federal interest for projects to be carried out under this section.”
; and

in subsection (f) by striking “$100,000,000” and inserting “$100,000,000, of which not more than $15,000,000 may be used to provide planning, design, and construction assistance to the Florida Keys Aqueduct Authority for a water treatment plant, Florida City, Florida”.

section.heading: LAKE WORTH, FLORIDA.
section.content: The Secretary may carry out necessary repairs for the Lake Worth bulkhead replacement project, West Palm Beach, Florida, at an estimated total cost of $9,000,000.

section.heading: BIG CREEK, GEORGIA, WATERSHED MANAGEMENT AND RESTORATION PROGRAM.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may cooperate with, by providing technical, planning, and construction assistance to, the city of Roswell, Georgia, as the non-Federal interest and coordinator with other local governments in the Big Creek watershed, Georgia, to assess the quality and quantity of water resources, conduct comprehensive watershed management planning, develop and implement water efficiency technologies and programs, and plan, design, and construct water resource facilities to restore the watershed.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary $5,000,000 to carry out this section.

section.heading: METROPOLITAN NORTH GEORGIA WATER PLANNING DISTRICT.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Program.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall establish a program to provide environmental assistance to non-Federal interests in the Metropolitan North Georgia Water Planning District.

subsection.heading: Form of Assistance.—
subsection.content: Assistance provided under this section may be in the form of design and construction assistance for water-related environmental infrastructure and resource protection and development projects in north Georgia, including projects for wastewater treatment and related facilities, elimination or control of combined sewer overflows, water supply and related facilities, environmental restoration, and surface water resource protection and development.

subsection.heading: Ownership Requirement.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may provide assistance for a project under this section only if the project is publicly owned.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Before providing assistance under this section, the Secretary shall enter into a partnership agreement with a non-Federal interest to provide for design and construction of the project to be carried out with the assistance.

paragraph.heading: Requirements.—
paragraph.chapeau: Each partnership agreement for a project entered into under this subsection shall provide for the following:

subparagraph.heading: Plan.—
subparagraph.content: Development by the Secretary, in consultation with appropriate Federal and State officials, of a facilities or resource protection and development plan, including appropriate engineering plans and specifications.

subparagraph.heading: Legal and institutional structures.—
subparagraph.content: Establishment of such legal and institutional structures as are necessary to ensure the effective long-term operation of the project by the non-Federal interest.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Federal share of the cost of a project under this section—

clause.content: shall be 75 percent; and
may be provided in the form of grants or reimbursements of project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for work.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall credit, in accordance with section 221 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d–5b), toward the non-Federal share of the cost of a project under this section, in an amount not to exceed 6 percent of the total construction costs of the project, the cost of design work carried out by the non-Federal interest for the project before the date of the partnership agreement for the project.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for interest.—
subparagraph.content: In case of a delay in the funding of the non-Federal share of the costs of a project that is the subject of an agreement under this section, the non-Federal interest shall receive credit for reasonable interest incurred in providing the non-Federal share.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for land, easements, and rights-of-way.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal interest shall receive credit for land, easements, rights-of-way, and relocations toward the non-Federal share of project costs (including all reasonable costs associated with obtaining permits necessary for the construction, operation, and maintenance of the project on publicly owned or controlled land), but the credit may not exceed 25 percent of total project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Operation and maintenance.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal share of operation and maintenance costs for projects constructed with assistance provided under this section shall be 100 percent.

subsection.heading: Applicability of Other Federal and State Laws.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section shall be construed to waive, limit, or otherwise affect the applicability of any provision of Federal or State law that would otherwise apply to a project to be carried out with assistance provided under this section.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $20,000,000.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: After completion of a Savannah Riverfront plan, the Secretary may participate in the ecosystem restoration, recreation, navigation, and flood damage reduction components of the plan.

subsection.heading: Coordination.—
subsection.content: In carrying out this section, the Secretary shall coordinate with appropriate representatives in the vicinity of Savannah, Georgia, including the Georgia Ports Authority, the city of Savannah, and Camden County.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated $10,000,000 to carry out this section.

section.heading: IDAHO, MONTANA, RURAL NEVADA, NEW MEXICO, RURAL UTAH, AND WYOMING.

subsection.chapeau: Section 595 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1999 (113 Stat. 383; 117 Stat. 139; 117 Stat. 142; 117 Stat. 1836; 118 Stat. 440) is amended—

paragraph.content: in the section heading by striking “AND RURAL UTAH” and inserting “RURAL UTAH, AND WYOMING”;
in subsections (b) and (c) by striking “and rural Utah” each place it appears and inserting “rural Utah, and Wyoming”; and

by striking subsection (h) and inserting the following:
“(h) Authorization of Appropriations.—There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section for the period beginning with fiscal year 2001 $150,000,000 for rural Nevada, $25,000,000 for each of Montana and New Mexico, $55,000,000 for Idaho, $50,000,000 for rural Utah, and $30,000,000 for Wyoming. Such sums shall remain available until expended.” .

section.heading: RILEY CREEK RECREATION AREA, IDAHO.
section.content: The Secretary is authorized to carry out the Riley Creek Recreation Area Operation Plan of the Albeni Falls Management Plan, dated October 2001, for the Riley Creek Recreation Area, Albeni Falls Dam, Bonner County, Idaho.

section.heading: FLOODPLAIN MAPPING, LITTLE CALUMET RIVER, CHICAGO, ILLINOIS.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall provide assistance for a project to develop maps identifying 100- and 500-year flood inundation areas along the Little Calumet River, Chicago, Illinois.

subsection.heading: Requirements.—
subsection.content: Maps developed under the project shall include hydrologic and hydraulic information and shall accurately show the flood inundation of each property by flood risk in the floodplain. The maps shall be produced in a high resolution format and shall be made available to all flood prone areas along the Little Calumet River, Chicago, Illinois, in an electronic format.

subsection.heading: Participation of FEMA.—
subsection.content: The Secretary and the non-Federal interests for the project shall work with the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency to ensure the validity of the maps developed under the project for flood insurance purposes.

subsection.heading: Forms of Assistance.—
subsection.content: In carrying out the project, the Secretary may enter into contracts or cooperative agreements with the non-Federal interests or provide reimbursements of project costs.

subsection.heading: Federal Share.—
subsection.content: The Federal share of the cost of the project shall be 50 percent.

subsection.heading: Limitation on Statutory Construction.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section shall be construed to modify the prioritization of map updates or the substantive requirements of the Federal Emergency Management Agency flood map modernization program authorized by section 1360 of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4101).

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $2,000,000.

section.heading: RECONSTRUCTION OF ILLINOIS AND MISSOURI FLOOD PROTECTION PROJECTS.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may participate in the reconstruction of an eligible flood control project if the Secretary determines that such reconstruction is not required as a result of improper operation and maintenance of the project by the non-Federal interest.

subsection.heading: Cost Sharing.—
subsection.content: The non-Federal share of the costs for the reconstruction of a flood control project authorized by this section shall be the same non-Federal share that was applicable to construction of the project. The non-Federal interest shall be responsible for operation and maintenance and repair of a project for which reconstruction is undertaken under this section.

subsection.heading: Reconstruction Defined.—
subsection.content: In this section, the term “reconstruction”, as used with respect to a project, means addressing major project deficiencies caused by long-term degradation of the foundation, construction materials, or engineering systems or components of the project, the results of which render the project at risk of not performing in compliance with its authorized project purposes. In addressing such deficiencies, the Secretary may incorporate current design standards and efficiency improvements, including the replacement of obsolete mechanical and electrical components at pumping stations, if such incorporation does not significantly change the scope, function, and purpose of the project as authorized.

subsection.heading: Eligible Projects.—
subsection.chapeau: The following flood control projects are eligible for reconstruction under this section:

paragraph.content: Clear Creek Drainage and Levee District, Illinois.
Fort Chartres and Ivy Landing Drainage District, Illinois.
Prairie Du Pont Levee and Sanitary District, including Fish Lake Drainage and Levee District, Illinois.
Cairo, Illinois Mainline Levee, Cairo, Illinois.
Goose Pond Pump Station, Cairo, Illinois.
Cottonwood Slough Pump Station, Alexander County, Illinois.
10th and 28th Street Pump Stations, Cairo, Illinois.
Flood control levee projects in Brookport, Shawneetown, Old Shawneetown, Golconda, Rosiclare, Harrisburg, and Reevesville, Illinois.
City of St. Louis, Missouri.
Missouri River Levee Drainage District, Missouri.

subsection.heading: Justification.—
subsection.content: The reconstruction of a project authorized by this section shall not be considered a separable element of the project.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated $50,000,000 to carry out this section.

subsection.heading: Extension of Authorization.—
subsection.content: Section 519(c)(2) of the Water Resources Development Act of 2000 (114 Stat. 2654) is amended by striking “2004” and inserting “2010”.

subsection.heading: Maximum Federal Share.—
subsection.content: Section 519(c)(3) of such Act (114 Stat. 2654) is amended by striking “$5,000,000” and inserting “$20,000,000”.

subsection.heading: In-Kind Services.—
subsection.content: Section 519(g)(3) of such Act (114 Stat. 2655) is amended by inserting before the period at the end of the first sentence “if such services are provided not more than 5 years before the date of initiation of the project or activity”.

subsection.heading: Monitoring.—
subsection.content:
Section 519 of such Act (114 Stat. 2654) is amended by adding at the end the following:
“(h) Monitoring.—The Secretary shall develop an Illinois River basin monitoring program to support the plan developed under subsection (b). Data collected under the monitoring program shall incorporate data provided by the State of Illinois and shall be publicly accessible through electronic means, including on the Internet.” .

section.heading: PROMONTORY POINT THIRD-PARTY REVIEW, CHICAGO SHORELINE, CHICAGO, ILLINOIS.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall conduct a third-party review of the Promontory Point feature of the project for storm damage reduction and shoreline erosion protection, Lake Michigan, Illinois, from Wilmette, Illinois, to the Illinois-Indiana State line, authorized by section 101(a)(12) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1996 (110 Stat. 3664), at a cost not to exceed $450,000.

paragraph.heading: Joint review.—
paragraph.content: The Buffalo and Seattle Districts of the Corps of Engineers shall jointly conduct the review under paragraph (1).

paragraph.heading: Standards.—
paragraph.content: The review under paragraph (1) shall be based on the standards under part 68 of title 36, Code of Federal Regulations (or any successor regulation).

subsection.heading: Contributions.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may accept funds from a State or political subdivision of a State to conduct the review under paragraph (1).

subsection.heading: Treatment.—
subsection.content: The review under paragraph (1) shall not be considered to be an element of the project referred to in paragraph (1).

subsection.heading: Effect of Section.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section shall be construed to affect the authorization for the project referred to in paragraph (1).

subsection.heading: Kaskaskia River Basin Defined.—
subsection.content: In this section, the term “Kaskaskia River Basin” means the Kaskaskia River, Illinois, its backwaters, its side channels, and all tributaries, including their watersheds, draining into the Kaskaskia River.

paragraph.heading: Development.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall develop, as expeditiously as practicable, a comprehensive plan for the purpose of restoring, preserving, and protecting the Kaskaskia River Basin.

paragraph.heading: Technologies and innovative approaches.—
paragraph.chapeau: The comprehensive plan shall provide for the development of new technologies and innovative approaches—

subparagraph.content: to enhance the Kaskaskia River as a transportation corridor;
to improve water quality within the entire Kaskaskia River Basin;
to restore, enhance, and preserve habitat for plants and wildlife;
to ensure aquatic integrity of side channels and backwaters and their connectivity with the mainstem river;
to increase economic opportunity for agriculture and business communities; and
to reduce the impacts of flooding to communities and landowners.

paragraph.heading: Specific components.—
paragraph.chapeau: The comprehensive plan shall include such features as are necessary to provide for—

subparagraph.content: the development and implementation of a program for sediment removal technology, sediment characterization, sediment transport, and beneficial uses of sediment;

the development and implementation of a program for the planning, conservation, evaluation, and construction of measures for fish and wildlife habitat conservation and rehabilitation, and stabilization and enhancement of land and water resources in the Kaskaskia River Basin;
the development and implementation of a long-term resource monitoring program for the Basin;

a conveyance study of the Kaskaskia River floodplain from Vandalia, Illinois, to Carlyle Lake to determine the impacts of existing and future waterfowl improvements on flood stages, including detailed surveys and mapping information to ensure proper hydraulic and hydrological analysis;
the development and implementation of a computerized inventory and analysis system for the Basin;
the development and implementation of a systemic plan for the Basin to reduce flood impacts by means of ecosystem restoration projects; and

the study and design of necessary measures to reduce ongoing headcutting and restore the aquatic environment of the Basin that has been degraded by the headcutting that has occurred above the existing grade control structure.

paragraph.heading: Consultation.—
paragraph.content: The comprehensive plan shall be developed by the Secretary in consultation with appropriate Federal agencies, the State of Illinois, and the Kaskaskia River Watershed Association.

paragraph.heading: Report to congress.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate a report containing the comprehensive plan.

paragraph.heading: Additional studies and analyses.—
paragraph.content: After submission of a report under paragraph (5), the Secretary shall conduct studies and analyses of projects related to the comprehensive plan that are appropriate and consistent with this subsection.

paragraph.heading: Water quality.—
paragraph.content: In carrying out activities under this section, the Secretary's recommendations shall be consistent with applicable State water quality standards.

paragraph.heading: Public participation.—
paragraph.content: In developing the comprehensive plan under subsection (b), the Secretary shall implement procedures to facilitate public participation, including providing advance notice of meetings, providing adequate opportunity for public input and comment, maintaining appropriate records, and making a record of the proceedings of meetings available for public inspection.

subsection.heading: Critical Projects and Initiatives.—
subsection.content: If the Secretary, in cooperation with appropriate Federal agencies and the State of Illinois, determines that a project or initiative for the Kaskaskia River Basin will produce independent, immediate, and substantial benefits, the Secretary may proceed with the implementation of the project.

subsection.heading: Coordination.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall integrate activities carried out under this section with ongoing Federal and State programs, projects, and activities, including the following:

paragraph.content: Farm programs of the Department of Agriculture.
Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (State of Illinois) and Conservation 2000 Ecosystem Program of the Illinois department of natural resources.
Conservation 2000 Conservation Practices Program and the Livestock Management Facilities Act administered by the Illinois department of agriculture.
National Buffer Initiative of the Natural Resources Conservation Service.
Nonpoint source grant program administered by the Illinois environmental protection agency.

Other programs that may be developed by the State of Illinois or the Federal Government, or that are carried out by nonprofit organizations, to carry out the objectives of the Kaskaskia River Basin Comprehensive Plan.

subsection.heading: In-Kind Services.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may credit the cost of in-kind services provided by the non-Federal interest for an activity carried out under this section toward not more than 80 percent of the non-Federal share of the cost of the activity. In-kind services shall include all State funds expended on programs that accomplish the goals of this section, as determined by the Secretary. The programs may include the Kaskaskia River Conservation Reserve Program, the Illinois Conservation 2000 Program, the Open Lands Trust Fund, and other appropriate programs carried out in the Kaskaskia River Basin.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated $20,000,000 to carry out this section.

subsection.heading: Southwest Illinois Defined.—
subsection.content: In this section, the term “Southwest Illinois” means the counties of Madison, St. Clair, Monroe, Randolph, Perry, Franklin, Jackson, Union, Alexander, Pulaski, and Williamson, Illinois.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Program.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may establish a program to provide environmental assistance to non-Federal interests in Southwest Illinois.

subsection.heading: Form of Assistance.—
subsection.content: Assistance provided under this section may be in the form of design and construction assistance for water-related environmental infrastructure and resource protection and development projects in Southwest Illinois, including projects for wastewater treatment and related facilities, water supply and related facilities, and surface water resource protection and development.

subsection.heading: Ownership Requirement.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may provide assistance for a project under this section only if the project is publicly owned.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Before providing assistance under this section, the Secretary shall enter into a partnership agreement with a non-Federal interest to provide for design and construction of the project to be carried out with the assistance.

paragraph.heading: Requirements.—
paragraph.chapeau: Each partnership agreement for a project entered into under this subsection shall provide for the following:

subparagraph.heading: Plan.—
subparagraph.content: Development by the Secretary, in consultation with appropriate Federal and State officials, of a facilities or resource protection and development plan, including appropriate engineering plans and specifications.

subparagraph.heading: Legal and institutional structures.—
subparagraph.content: Establishment of such legal and institutional structures as are necessary to ensure the effective long-term operation of the project by the non-Federal interest.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Federal share of the cost of a project under this section—

clause.content: shall be 75 percent; and
may be provided in the form of grants or reimbursements of project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for work.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall credit, in accordance with section 221 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d–5b), toward the non-Federal share of the cost of the project the cost of design work carried out by the non-Federal interest for the project before the date of the partnership agreement for the project.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for interest.—
subparagraph.content: In case of a delay in the funding of the non-Federal share of a project that is the subject of an agreement under this section, the non-Federal interest shall receive credit for reasonable interest incurred in providing the non-Federal share.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for land, easements, and rights-of-way.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal interest shall receive credit for land, easements, rights-of-way, and relocations toward the non-Federal share of project costs (including all reasonable costs associated with obtaining permits necessary for the construction, operation, and maintenance of the project on publicly owned or controlled land), but the credit may not exceed 25 percent of total project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Operation and maintenance.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal share of operation and maintenance costs for projects constructed with assistance provided under this section shall be 100 percent.

subsection.heading: Applicability of Other Federal and State Laws.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section shall be construed to waive, limit, or otherwise affect the applicability of any provision of Federal or State law that would otherwise apply to a project to be carried out with assistance provided under this section.

subsection.heading: Nonprofit Entities.—
subsection.content: In accordance with section 221(b) of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d–5b(b)), for any project carried out under this section, a non-Federal interest may include a nonprofit entity with the consent of the affected local government.

subsection.heading: Corps of Engineers Expenses.—
subsection.content: Not more than 10 percent of the amounts appropriated to carry out this section may be used by the Corps of Engineers district offices to administer projects under this section at Federal expense.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $40,000,000.

subsection.chapeau: Section 219(f)(12) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1992 (113 Stat. 335; 117 Stat. 1843) is amended—

paragraph.content:
by adding at the end the following:
“(B) Credit.—The Secretary shall credit, in accordance with section 221 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d–5b), toward the non-Federal share of the cost of the project the cost of planning and design work carried out by the non-Federal interest for the project before the date of the partnership agreement for the project.” ; and
by aligning the remainder of the text of subparagraph (A) (as designated by paragraph (1) of this section) with subparagraph (B) (as added by paragraph (2) of this section).

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall provide assistance for a project to develop maps identifying 100- and 500-year flood inundation areas in the State of Iowa, along the Missouri River.

subsection.heading: Requirements.—
subsection.content: Maps developed under the project shall include hydrologic and hydraulic information and shall accurately portray the flood hazard areas in the floodplain. The maps shall be produced in a high resolution format and shall be made available to the State of Iowa in an electronic format.

subsection.heading: Participation of FEMA.—
subsection.content: The Secretary and the non-Federal interests for the project shall work with the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency to ensure the validity of the maps developed under the project for flood insurance purposes.

subsection.heading: Forms of Assistance.—
subsection.content: In carrying out the project, the Secretary may enter into contracts or cooperative agreements with the non-Federal interests or provide reimbursements of project costs.

subsection.heading: Federal Share.—
subsection.content: The Federal share of the cost of the project shall be 50 percent.

subsection.heading: Limitation on Statutory Construction.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section shall be construed to modify the prioritization of map updates or the substantive requirements of the Federal Emergency Management Agency flood map modernization program authorized by section 1360 of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4101).

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $3,000,000.

section.heading: PADUCAH, KENTUCKY.
section.content: The Secretary shall complete a feasibility report for rehabilitation of the project for flood damage reduction, Paducah, Kentucky, authorized by section 4 of the Flood Control Act of June 28, 1938 (52 Stat. 1217), and, if the Secretary determines that the project is feasible, the Secretary may carry out the project at a total cost of $3,000,000.

section.heading: SOUTHERN AND EASTERN KENTUCKY.
section.content:
Section 531 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1996 (110 Stat. 3773; 113 Stat. 348; 117 Stat. 142) is amended by adding at the end the following:
“(i) Corps of Engineers Expenses.—Not more than 10 percent of the amounts appropriated to carry out this section may be used by the Corps of Engineers district offices to administer projects under this section at Federal expense.” .

section.heading: WINCHESTER, KENTUCKY.
section.content:
Section 219(c) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1992 (106 Stat. 4835; 114 Stat. 2763A–219) is amended by adding at the end the following:
“(41) Winchester, kentucky.—Wastewater infrastructure, Winchester, Kentucky.” .

section.heading: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA.
section.content: Section 219(f)(21) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1992 (113 Stat. 336; 114 Stat. 2763A–220) is amended by striking “$20,000,000” and inserting “$35,000,000”.

section.heading: CALCASIEU SHIP CHANNEL, LOUISIANA.
section.content: The Secretary shall expedite completion of a dredged material management plan for the Calcasieu Ship Channel, Louisiana, and may take interim measures to increase the capacity of existing disposal areas, or to construct new confined or beneficial use disposal areas, for the channel.

section.heading: EAST ATCHAFALAYA BASIN AND AMITE RIVER BASIN REGION, LOUISIANA.

subsection.content: In this section, the term “East Atchafalaya Basin and Amite River Basin Region” means the following parishes and municipalities in the State of Louisiana: Ascension, East Baton Rouge, East Feliciana, Iberville, Livingston, Pointe Coupee, St. Helena, West Baton Rouge, and West Feliciana.

subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $45,000,000.

section.heading: INNER HARBOR NAVIGATION CANAL LOCK PROJECT, LOUISIANA.

subsection.chapeau: Not later than July 1, 2008, the Secretary shall—

paragraph.content: issue a final environmental impact statement relating to the Inner Harbor Navigation Canal Lock project, Louisiana; and

paragraph.chapeau: develop and maintain a transportation mitigation program relating to that project in coordination with—

subparagraph.content: St. Bernard Parish;
Orleans Parish;
the Old Arabi Neighborhood Association; and
other interested parties.

section.heading: LAKE PONTCHARTRAIN, LOUISIANA.
section.content: For purposes of carrying out section 121 of the Federal Water Pollution Control Act (33 U.S.C. 1273), the Lake Pontchartrain, Louisiana, basin stakeholders conference convened by the Environmental Protection Agency, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and United States Geological Survey on February 25, 2002, shall be treated as being a management conference convened under section 320 of such Act (33 U.S.C. 1330).

subsection.heading: Definition of Southeast Louisiana Region.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section, the term “Southeast Louisiana Region” means any of the following parishes and municipalities in the State of Louisiana:

paragraph.content: Orleans.
Jefferson.
St. Tammany.
Tangipahoa.
St. Bernard.
St. Charles.
St. John.
Plaquemines.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Program.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may establish a program to provide environmental assistance to non-Federal interests in the Southeast Louisiana Region.

subsection.heading: Form of Assistance.—
subsection.content: Assistance provided under this section may be in the form of design and construction assistance for water-related environmental infrastructure and resource protection and development projects in the Southeast Louisiana Region, including projects for wastewater treatment and related facilities, water supply and related facilities, environmental restoration, and surface water resource protection and development (including projects to improve water quality in the Lake Pontchartrain basin).

subsection.heading: Corps of Engineers Expenses.—

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $22,000,000.

subsection.heading: Modification of Study.—
subsection.content: The study for the project for waterfront and riverine preservation, restoration, and enhancement, Mississippi River, West Baton Rouge Parish, Louisiana, being carried out under Committee Resolution 2570 of the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives adopted July 23, 1998, is modified to add West Feliciana Parish and East Baton Rouge Parish to the geographic scope of the study.

subsection.heading: Construction.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may, upon completion of the study, participate in the ecosystem restoration, navigation, flood damage reduction, and recreation components of the project.

subsection.heading: Credit.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall credit, in accordance with section 221 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d–5b), toward the non-Federal share of the cost of the project the cost of design work carried out by the non-Federal interest for the project before the date of the partnership agreement for the project.

subsection.heading: Expedited Consideration.—
subsection.content:
Section 517(5) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1999 (113 Stat. 345) is amended to read as follows:
“(5) Mississippi River, West Baton Rouge, West Feliciana, and East Baton Rouge Parishes, Louisiana, project for waterfront and riverine preservation, restoration, and enhancement modifications.” .

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $10,000,000.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may carry out a project for nonstructural flood damage reduction and ecosystem restoration at Charlestown, Maryland.

subsection.heading: Land Acquisition.—
subsection.content: The flood damage reduction component of the project may include the acquisition of private property from willing sellers.

subsection.heading: Justification.—
subsection.content: Any nonstructural flood damage reduction project to be carried out under this section that will result in the conversion of property to use for ecosystem restoration and wildlife habitat shall be justified based on national ecosystem restoration benefits.

subsection.heading: Use of Acquired Property.—
subsection.content: Property acquired under this section shall be maintained in public ownership for ecosystem restoration and wildlife habitat.

subsection.heading: Ability to Pay.—
subsection.content: In determining the appropriate non-Federal cost share for the project, the Secretary shall determine the ability of Cecil County, Maryland, to participate as a cost-sharing non-Federal interest in accordance with section 103(m) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (33 U.S.C. 2213(m)).

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated $2,000,000 to carry out this section.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall carry out the project for shoreline protection, St. Mary's River, Maryland, under section 3 of the Act entitled “An Act authorizing Federal participation in the cost of protecting the shores of publicly owned property”, approved August 13, 1946 (33 U.S.C. 426g).

subsection.heading: Use of Funds.—
subsection.content: In carrying out the project under subsection (a), the Secretary shall use funds made available for such project under Energy and Water Development Appropriations Act, 2006 (Public Law 109–103).

section.heading: MASSACHUSETTS DREDGED MATERIAL DISPOSAL SITES.
section.content: The Secretary may cooperate with Massachusetts in the management and long-term monitoring of aquatic dredged material disposal sites within the State and is authorized to accept funds from the State to carry out such activities.

section.heading: ONTONAGON HARBOR, MICHIGAN.
section.content: The Secretary shall conduct a study of shore damage in the vicinity of the project for navigation, Ontonagon Harbor, Ontonagon County, Michigan, authorized by section 101 of the Rivers and Harbors Act of 1962 (76 Stat. 1176) and reauthorized by section 363 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1996 (110 Stat. 3730), to determine if the damage is the result of a Federal navigation project, and, if the Secretary determines that the damage is the result of a Federal navigation project, the Secretary shall carry out a project to mitigate the damage under section 111 of the River and Harbor Act of 1968 (33 U.S.C. 426i).

section.heading: CROOKSTON, MINNESOTA.
section.content: The Secretary shall conduct a study for a project for emergency streambank protection along the Red Lake River in Crookston, Minnesota, and, if the Secretary determines that the project is feasible, the Secretary may carry out the project under section 14 of the Flood Control Act of 1946 (33 U.S.C. 701r); except that the maximum amount of Federal funds that may be expended for the project shall be $6,500,000.

subsection.heading: Project Description.—
subsection.chapeau: Section 219(f)(61) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1992 (114 Stat. 2763A–221) is amended—

paragraph.content: in the paragraph heading by striking “and kathio township” and inserting “, crow wing county, mille lacs county, mille lacs indian reservation, and kathio township”;
by striking “$11,000,000” and inserting “$17,000,000”;
by inserting “, Crow Wing County, Mille Lacs County, Mille Lacs Indian Reservation established by the treaty of February 22, 1855 (10 Stat. 1165),” after “Garrison”; and

by adding at the end the following: “Such assistance shall be provided directly to the Garrison-Kathio-West Mille Lacs Lake Sanitary District, Minnesota, except for assistance provided directly to the Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe at the discretion of the Secretary.”.

subsection.heading: Procedures.—
subsection.content: In carrying out the project authorized by such section 219(f)(61), the Secretary may use the cost sharing and contracting procedures available to the Secretary under section 569 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1999 (113 Stat. 368).

section.heading: ITASCA COUNTY, MINNESOTA.
section.content: The Secretary shall carry out a project for flood damage reduction, Trout Lake and Canisteo Pit, Itasca County, Minnesota, without regard to normal policy considerations.

subsection.heading: Conveyance.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall convey to the city of Minneapolis by quitclaim deed and without consideration all right, title, and interest of the United States to the property known as the War Department (Fort Snelling Interceptor) Tunnel in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

subsection.heading: Applicability of Property Screening Provisions.—
subsection.content: Section 2696 of title 10, United States Code, shall not apply to the conveyance under this section.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: Section 569 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1999 (113 Stat. 368) is amended—

paragraph.content: in subsection (a) by striking “Benton, Sherburne,” and inserting “Beltrami, Hubbard, Wadena,”;
by striking the last sentence of subsection (e)(3)(B);
in subsection (h) by striking “$40,000,000” and inserting “$54,000,000”; and

by adding at the end the following:
“(i) Corps of Engineers Expenses.—Not more than 10 percent of the amounts appropriated to carry out this section may be used by the Corps of Engineers district offices to administer projects under this section at Federal expense.” .

subsection.heading: Biwabik, Minnesota.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall reimburse the non-Federal interest for the project for environmental infrastructure, Biwabik, Minnesota, carried out under section 569 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1999 (113 Stat. 368), for planning, design, and construction costs that were incurred by the non-Federal interest with respect to the project before the date of the partnership agreement for the project and that were in excess of the non-Federal share of the cost of the project if the Secretary determines that the costs are appropriate.

section.heading: WILD RICE RIVER, MINNESOTA.
section.content: The Secretary shall expedite the completion of the general reevaluation report, authorized by section 438 of the Water Resources Development Act of 2000 (114 Stat. 2640), for the project for flood protection, Wild Rice River, Minnesota, authorized by section 201 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (84 Stat. 1825), to develop alternatives to the Twin Valley Lake feature, and upon the completion of such report, shall construct the project at a total cost of $20,000,000.

section.heading: MISSISSIPPI.
section.content: Section 592(g) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1999 (113 Stat. 380; 117 Stat. 1837) is amended by striking “$100,000,000” and inserting “$110,000,000”.

section.heading: HARRISON, HANCOCK, AND JACKSON COUNTIES, MISSISSIPPI.
section.content: In carrying out projects for the protection, restoration, and creation of aquatic and ecologically related habitats located in Harrison, Hancock, and Jackson Counties, Mississippi, under section 204 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1992 (33 U.S.C. 2326), the Secretary shall accept any portion of the non-Federal share of the cost of the projects in the form of in-kind services and materials.

section.heading: MISSISSIPPI RIVER, MISSOURI AND ILLINOIS.
section.content: As a part of the operation and maintenance of the project for the Mississippi River (Regulating Works), between the Ohio and Missouri Rivers, Missouri and Illinois, authorized by the first section of an Act entitled “Making appropriations for the construction, repair, and preservation of certain public works on rivers and harbors, and for other purposes”, approved June 25, 1910 (36 Stat. 630), the Secretary may carry out activities necessary to restore and protect fish and wildlife habitat in the middle Mississippi River system. Such activities may include modification of navigation training structures, modification and creation of side channels, modification and creation of islands, and studies and analysis necessary to apply adaptive management principles in design of future work.

subsection.chapeau: Section 219(f)(32) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1992 (113 Stat. 337) is amended—

paragraph.content: by striking “a project” and inserting “projects”;
by striking “$15,000,000” and inserting “$35,000,000”; and
by inserting “and St. Louis County” before “, Missouri”.

section.heading: ST. LOUIS REGIONAL GREENWAYS, ST. LOUIS, MISSOURI.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may participate in the ecosystem restoration, recreation, and flood damage reduction components of the St. Louis Regional Greenways Proposal of the Metropolitan Park and Recreation District, St. Louis, Missouri, dated March 31, 2004.

subsection.heading: Coordination.—
subsection.content: In carrying out this section, the Secretary shall coordinate with appropriate representatives in the vicinity of St. Louis, Missouri, including the Metropolitan Park and Recreation District, the city of St. Louis, St. Louis County, and St. Charles County.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated $10,000,000 to carry out this section.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may participate in the ecosystem restoration, flood damage reduction, and recreation components of the Clark Fork River Revitalization Project, Missoula, Montana.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated $5,000,000 to carry out this section.

section.heading: ST. MARY PROJECT, GLACIER COUNTY, MONTANA.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary, in consultation with the Bureau of Reclamation, shall conduct all necessary studies, develop an emergency response plan, provide technical and planning and design assistance, and rehabilitate and construct the St. Mary Diversion and Conveyance Works project located within the exterior boundaries of the Blackfeet Reservation in the State of Montana, at a total cost of $153,000,000.

subsection.heading: Federal Share.—
subsection.content: The Federal share of the total cost of the project under this section shall be 75 percent.

subsection.heading: Participation by Blackfeet Tribe and Fort Belknap Indian Community.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Except as provided in paragraph (2), no construction shall be carried out under this section until the earlier of—

subparagraph.content: the date on which Congress approves the reserved water rights settlements of the Blackfeet Tribe and the Fort Belknap Indian Community; and
January 1, 2011.

paragraph.heading: Exception.—
paragraph.chapeau: Paragraph (1) shall not apply with respect to construction relating to—

subparagraph.content: standard operation and maintenance; or
emergency repairs to ensure water transportation or the protection of life and property.

paragraph.heading: Requirement.—
paragraph.content: The Blackfeet Tribe shall be a participant in all phases of the project authorized by this section.

section.heading: LOWER PLATTE RIVER WATERSHED RESTORATION, NEBRASKA.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary may cooperate with and provide assistance to the Lower Platte River natural resources districts in the State of Nebraska to serve as non-Federal interests with respect to—

paragraph.content: conducting comprehensive watershed planning in the natural resource districts;
assessing water resources in the natural resource districts; and

providing project feasibility planning, design, and construction assistance for water resource and watershed management in the natural resource districts, including projects for environmental restoration and flood damage reduction.

paragraph.heading: Federal share.—
paragraph.content: The Federal share of the cost of carrying out an activity described in subsection (a)(1) shall be 75 percent.

paragraph.heading: Non-federal share.—
paragraph.content: The non-Federal share of the cost of carrying out an activity described in subsection (a) may be provided in cash or in kind.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section $12,000,000.

paragraph.chapeau: in subsection (a)—

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
